finding: The workspace "shared theme" push moves CSS rules, not design tokens: it writes Site.projectStyles, while a site's brand lives in a different column (projectSettings.designTokens) that the push never touches — so an agency pushing its brand changes no colour, font or spacing on any client site.
evidence: theme.service.ts:10-11 says 'captures one site's tokens as Workspace.sharedTheme, then pushes that token set onto its client sites' projectStyles'; captureSharedTheme reads `select: { projectStyles: true }` (theme.service.ts:79) and pushSharedTheme writes `projectStyles: styles` (theme.service.ts:184). BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:310 states what that column actually is: 'projectStyles holds StyleEngine CSS rules ({id, selector, properties})'. Brand's Apply writes tokens to `designTokens` inside projectSettings (DesignSystemTab.tsx:539-543), a field pushSharedTheme never names.
fix: Make the shared theme carry `projectSettings.designTokens` + `designTokensSchemaVersion` (and `designPresets` once MOD-F-06 is fixed), not `projectStyles`. Capture from projectSettings, push into projectSettings, snapshot projectSettings for rollback.
chain: Brand -> DesignToken -> Apply -> (theme.capture/push) -> Dashboard agency theme -> Client sites' tokens change

finding: The same push is destructive on the receiving side: projectStyles is a list of element-id-keyed CSS rules (`[data-buildrick-id="<id>"]`), so pushing site A's rules onto site B overwrites B's own responsive/pseudo styles with rules that target element ids that do not exist on B.
evidence: StyleEngine writes per-element rules as `const selector = `[data-buildrick-id="${elementId}"]`` (StyleEngine.ts:222,245,270) and exportStyles returns that whole map (StyleEngine.ts:426-428); Composer.exportProject sends it as `styles` (Composer.ts:615) which sites.service.ts:728 stores into projectStyles. pushSharedTheme replaces the target's projectStyles wholesale (theme.service.ts:184).
fix: Do not ship element-scoped rules across sites at all. If MOD-F-01 is fixed the push carries tokens only; if projectStyles must move, filter to class/global selectors and merge rather than replace.
chain: Brand -> StyleEngine rules -> theme.push -> Client site -> that site's breakpoint + hover styles are deleted

finding: Both ends of the shared-theme feature call it "tokens" in the UI while moving CSS rules, and the capture error tells the user to do the one thing that cannot fix it.
evidence: Dashboard: 'Every following site adopts this theme's tokens.' (theme-manager.tsx:207) and 'Undo — restore the tokens this site had before the push' (theme-manager.tsx:48). Editor: 'Everyday styling lives here. The brand syncs from your workspace shared theme.' (DesignSystemTab.tsx:659). captureSharedTheme throws 'That site has no styles to capture yet — open it, set your brand colours and type, then capture.' (theme.service.ts:91) on `site.projectStyles == null` — but setting brand colours and type writes designTokens (DesignSystemTab.tsx:541), never projectStyles, so following the instruction leaves the error in place.
fix: After MOD-F-01, the copy becomes true. Until then the capture error must name what it actually needs (a saved style rule), and the Brand strip must not claim a sync that does not exist (already filed as W-G-03).
chain: Brand -> copy -> user follows it -> capture still fails -> agency theme never captured

finding: A theme push bumps dsSchemaVersion specifically 'so an open editor reloads tokens', and no editor code reads dsSchemaVersion after load — an editor open during a push never learns, and its next save overwrites the push.
evidence: theme.service.ts:136 comment + `dsSchemaVersion: site.dsSchemaVersion + 1` (theme.service.ts:186). The only editor reads are at load: BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:327 and useComposerInit.ts:193. No listener, no poll, no SSE. The editor's own save then writes projectStyles back from StyleEngine (sites.service.ts:728).
fix: Either push a server event the open editor subscribes to, or have the editor re-read dsSchemaVersion before each save and refuse/merge on a bump.
chain: Brand -> dsSchemaVersion -> theme.push -> Editor (open session) -> nothing reacts -> next autosave reverts the push

finding: DS project migrations are fed the wrong array: the runner is handed `data.styles` (CSS rules) as `project.tokens`, so migration 0003 appends a design-token record into the site's CSS-rule list and no token is ever migrated.
evidence: useComposerInit.ts:196 `project: { tokens: (data.styles ?? []) as unknown as DesignToken[] }` and :202 writes the result back as `styles: result.project.tokens`. migration0003.up appends WARNING_TOKEN to `project.tokens` (0003-add-color-warning.ts:52-53) and its own header says the target is 'projects loaded from a saved designTokens payload' (:8-9). BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:316-325 has already filtered every token-shaped entry OUT of `styles`, so the array the runner receives can never contain a token. dsSchemaVersion is then bumped to 3, so it never runs again.
fix: Feed the runner `settings.designTokens` and write the result back to settings, or delete the engine-side projectMigrations framework — `mergeProjectTokens` over DEFAULT_TOKENS (projectTokens.ts:33) already guarantees color-warning is present, which is why nobody noticed.
chain: Brand -> DesignToken -> project load -> MigrationManager -> a token record is injected into projectStyles and StyleEngine drops it

finding: Style presets (11 categories, the whole Brand › Styles destination) are written to projectSettings.designPresets and read by nothing — the only hydration source is localStorage, so every preset edit is device-local and dies with a cache clear or on any other machine.
evidence: Write: DesignSystemTab.tsx:543 `designPresets: presetRecords`. Read: `grep -rn designPresets` across server/, packages/ returns exactly two hits — the type at project.ts:259 and that write. Hydration is `localStorage.getItem(storageKey)` where storageKey = `buildrick-design-presets-${projectId}-v1` (StylePresetRegistryContext.tsx:55,61), falling back to DEFAULT_PRESETS. persistAll writes only localStorage (:98).
fix: Seed StylePresetRegistryProvider from composer.getProjectSettings().designPresets the way ProjectTokensApplier/loadFromComposer do for tokens; keep localStorage as the offline cache, not the source.

finding: A style preset never reaches an element or the published page: nothing anywhere consumes StylePreset.bindings, so the eleven preset editors change a record and nothing else.
evidence: `StylePreset`/`bindings` consumers outside the registry + its own UI are: DSLinter.ts:174 (lints them) and nothing else. The export path emits tokens and fonts only — ExportEngine.ts:259-260 call siteTokensCSS/siteFontCSS on `designTokens`; no preset equivalent exists. usePresetsForCategory.ts:10 claims 'Apply runs through the containing context's persistAll → composer.setProjectSettings', which is true and inert.
fix: Either emit preset bindings as CSS in siteTokensCSS's neighbour and apply them to catalog elements, or mark Brand › Styles as not-yet-wired instead of offering Save.

finding: All eight orphan engine:styles events come from GlobalStyleManager, a manager with zero callers anywhere outside the Composer constructor — and it emits on its OWN EventEmitter, not the composer bus, so nothing could listen even if it wanted to.
evidence: GlobalStyleManager extends EventEmitter (GlobalStyleManager.ts:46) and fires `this.emit(...)` for STYLE_DEFINED :186, STYLE_UPDATED :216, STYLE_DELETED :240, STYLE_APPLIED :308, STYLE_CLASS_CREATED :324, STYLES_IMPORTED :388, STYLES_CLEARED :398. Grep for `globalStyles` across src/ + demo/ returns only Composer.ts:146,250,1092 (declare/construct/destroy) and barrel re-exports. StyleEngine.ts:726 still says 'This will be enhanced when GlobalStyleManager is integrated'. Its export()/import() are never called by Composer.exportProject (Composer.ts:611-624), so a global style would not survive a reload either.
fix: Delete GlobalStyleManager and the seven STYLE_* constants it owns, or wire it: route emits through `this.composer.emit`, add export()/import() to the project snapshot, and give it a panel. Keeping it costs 7 dead events and 7 built-in styles on every Composer.

finding: The dead GlobalStyleManager seeds every Composer with indigo #667eea built-ins named 'Primary Button' and 'Secondary Button' — a banned hue sitting one wire away from customer output.
evidence: GlobalStyleManager.ts:71,90,92 `background: "#667eea"` / `color: "#667eea"` / `border: "2px solid #667eea"`, registered unconditionally in registerDefaults (:62) from the constructor (:55). DESIGN.md bans purple/violet/indigo; the accent is #1A56DB.
fix: Delete with MOD-F-08. If any of it is revived, the values come from --buildrick-design-* tokens, not literals.

finding: Applying a starter is a single unconfirmed click that clears the per-token undo stacks for three registries, and the only route back (Discard) throws away every unrelated staged edit with it.
evidence: StartersSection.tsx:39-45 — `choose` calls applyStarter directly from the card, no confirm; useApplyStarter.ts:63-65 calls stageTokens on colour/spacing/type; useTokenBase.ts:143-144 `setUndoStack({}); setRedoStack({})`. handleDiscard (DesignSystemTab.tsx:559-575) runs discardAll on ALL 14 registries and 11 preset registries. Blast radius is bounded: savedTokens is untouched (:139-148 comment) so Discard does restore the last-applied values, and the canvas/preview/export all read the same designTokens.
fix: Confirm before applying (the board already warns; the confirm is what is missing — W-G-11), and make the toast's Undo restore only the starter's own diff instead of routing through Discard.
chain: Brand -> DesignToken -> apply starter -> Canvas + preview + export -> whole site repaints, per-token undo gone

finding: Starters stage only 3 of the 14 token kinds, so 'Applying a starter overwrites your tokens' overwrites a third of them and silently leaves radius, shadow, motion, border, opacity, z-index, breakpoint, grid, sizing, icon and imagery on the previous brand.
evidence: useApplyStarter.ts:63-65 stages colorRegistry, spacingRegistry, typeRegistry only. DesignSystemTab aggregates 14 registries (imports at :29-45, `allRegistries`), and persistAll persists all 14 (TokenRegistryContext.tsx:197 comment).
fix: Have starters declare all kinds they intend to set and stage every registry, or say in the warning which three groups change.

finding: The design-system lint runs over 3 of the 14 token registries, so 11 kinds can never produce a finding and the Lint destination's count is structurally incomplete.
evidence: useDSLint.ts:26-36 builds allTokens from useColorRegistry + useSpacingRegistry + useTypeRegistry only, and that array is what reaches composer.dsLinter.lint (:49). DSLintRunner mounts it once for the whole editor (StudioPanels.tsx:405).
fix: Pass every registry (the same `allRegistries` array DesignSystemTab already assembles) into useDSLint.

finding: Two independent schema-version counters exist for the same concept and neither knows about the other: Site.dsSchemaVersion (engine runner, target 3) and projectSettings.designTokensSchemaVersion (editor migrations, target 5).
evidence: Engine: TARGET_PROJECT_VERSION = 3 (projectMigrations/index.ts:19), consumed from `data.dsSchemaVersion` (useComposerInit.ts:193). Editor: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5 (design-system/migrations/index.ts:47), consumed from `settings.designTokensSchemaVersion` (DesignSystemTab.tsx:379, projectTokens.ts:30). Two migration registries, two `up`/`validate` conventions, one token payload.
fix: Retire the engine runner (see MOD-F-05) and keep designTokensSchemaVersion as the single counter, or make dsSchemaVersion a pure cache-buster with no migration semantics.

finding: localStorage is a second source of truth for tokens and it wins the first paint: the registry seeds from `buildrick-design-tokens-<projectId>-v1` and only the Brand panel's own mount reconciles it against the project.
evidence: TokenRegistryContext.tsx:114,122 seed from localStorage; ProjectTokensApplier only writes CSS custom properties (:50) and never resets registry state; the reset lives in DesignSystemTab.loadFromComposer → resetAllKinds (:398), which runs when the PANEL mounts.
fix: Move resetAllKinds into a headless applier alongside ProjectTokensApplier so registry state and CSS variables are reconciled at project load, not at panel open.

finding: BRAND_APPLIED has exactly one listener — the onboarding checklist — so applying a brand ticks a step and notifies nothing else: not the topbar, not autosave, not the canvas.
evidence: Emit: DesignSystemTab.tsx:554. Only listener: OnboardingMount.tsx:62 `{ id: "set-brand", event: EVENTS.BRAND_APPLIED }`. The comment at DesignSystemTab.tsx:363-368 explains that brand staging deliberately does NOT raise the project dirty flag, so the apply itself is the only moment the project could be told.
fix: On BRAND_APPLIED, mark the project dirty / trigger a save so applied tokens reach the server without waiting for an unrelated canvas edit.
chain: Brand -> DesignToken -> Apply -> BRAND_APPLIED -> Save/autosave -> tokens reach the server on their own

finding: All five component/instance events are strong orphans, and the one thing they exist for — telling the rest of the editor that instances changed — is done instead by physically deleting and re-pasting elements, so every count and badge that should react is stale until something unrelated re-renders it.
evidence: COMPONENT_INSTANTIATED (ComponentInstances.ts:114), INSTANCE_OVERRIDE (:151 and ComponentInstance.ts:166), INSTANCE_DETACHED (:194), INSTANCE_SYNCED (:306), INSTANCE_VARIANT_CHANGED (:413) — a repo-wide grep for each constant finds only the emit and the type map. The actual fan-out is syncAllInstances → syncInstance → composer.elements.removeElement + pasteElement (ComponentInstances.ts:274-288) plus markInstanceElementsDirty, which re-emits ELEMENT_UPDATED per node (ComponentVariantResolver.ts:103).
fix: Subscribe the three surfaces that display instance counts (ComponentDetailScreen.tsx:247, ComponentsTab.tsx:251, ComponentsSection.tsx:105) to COMPONENT_INSTANTIATED + INSTANCE_DETACHED + INSTANCE_SYNCED, and the inspector's VariantSection to INSTANCE_VARIANT_CHANGED.
chain: Components -> ComponentInstance -> instantiate/detach/sync -> COMPONENT_INSTANTIATED / INSTANCE_DETACHED / INSTANCE_SYNCED -> Components panel + Brand summary + Inspector -> counts and the instance band update

finding: updateComponentMaster is the one path that fans a master edit out to instances, and it emits COMPONENT_UPDATED but not COMPONENT_LIST_UPDATED — which is the only event the Components panel listens to, so the panel keeps rendering the pre-update definition.
evidence: ComponentManager.ts:275-278 emits COMPONENT_UPDATED alone; every other mutation pairs it with COMPONENT_LIST_UPDATED (:196, :229, :307, :384, :403). useComponentsState.ts:160 subscribes to COMPONENT_LIST_UPDATED only, and ComponentDetailScreen renders from the `component` object handed down from that list.
fix: Emit COMPONENT_LIST_UPDATED after the sync in updateComponentMaster, the way persistComponentEdit does.
chain: Components -> ComponentDefinition -> Update from selection -> COMPONENT_LIST_UPDATED -> Components panel -> the detail screen shows the new master and version

finding: Variant authoring has no caller, so component.variants is always empty and the variant UI is a chain of dead controls: the create modal collects variant properties, the inspector renders a Select per property, and selecting a value is a guaranteed no-op.
evidence: setVariantProperties (ComponentManager.ts:311), addVariant (:320), updateVariant (:331), removeVariant (:347) have zero non-test callers. variantProperties IS written — CreateComponentModal.tsx:92-101,107 passes it through createComponent (ComponentManager.ts:188) — so VariantSection renders a Select for each (VariantSection.tsx:124-139), and handleVariantChange looks up `variants.find(...)` in an always-empty array (:78-84) and returns silently. getVariantStylesForElement bails on `!component?.variants?.length` (ComponentVariantResolver.ts:130), so a variant could never render either.
fix: Either build the variant editor that calls addVariant/updateVariant, or stop offering the axes: hide the 'This is a variant set' block in CreateComponentModal and the property Selects in VariantSection until variants can exist. (Already filed as W-O-09/W-O-10/W-O-11; this row adds the code chain and the four zero-caller methods.)
chain: Components -> ComponentVariant -> addVariant -> (no caller) -> Inspector VariantSection + panel Swap-variant -> nothing ever selectable

finding: defaultVariantId is declared on every component and read nowhere — instantiateComponent creates instances with no variantSelection at all.
evidence: Declared at components.ts:43. instantiateComponent builds the instance literal without it (ComponentInstances.ts:103-109). Repo-wide grep for defaultVariantId outside the type finds no reader.
fix: Delete the field, or set `variantSelection: { variantId: component.defaultVariantId }` at instantiation once MOD-F-18 lands.

finding: The Save-as-component modal promises token binding it does not deliver twice over: the bindings are only ever counted, never persisted, and the resolver that produces the count matches a syntax the product no longer writes — so the hint always reads '0 styles will bind to your DS tokens.'
evidence: TokenBindingResolver matches only `/^\{\{token\.([a-zA-Z0-9._-]+)\}\}$/` (TokenBindingResolver.ts:23). TokenUsageTracker.ts:33-38 documents the same bug being fixed on its own side: '{{token.…}} only ever appears in template HTML strings, and resolveTemplateTokens substitutes those away before import… Everything a user binds through the UI is written as var(--buildrick-design-<id>)' — matching only the first form 'meant getUsage() returned 0 for every token in real use' (blocker A14). The resolver never got the second regex. The map then reaches only `bindingCount = selectionContext.extractedBindings.size` (CreateComponentModal.tsx:56), rendered as 'N styles will bind to your DS tokens. Editing tokens later updates this component too.' (:246-248); createComponent is called without it (:103-111), and ComponentDefinition has no bindings field. `prefillFromDs` is stored (ComponentManager.ts:189) and read by nothing — components.ts:44-47 admits 'UI today just records the user's intent.'
fix: Add TOKEN_VAR_RE to TokenBindingResolver (copy TokenUsageTracker.ts:49), and either persist the bindings on the definition and honour prefillFromDs, or replace the hint with copy that does not promise propagation.

finding: 'Save as component' on a multi-selection saves only the first element and says nothing — the handler deliberately collects every selected id and the modal drops all but one.
evidence: standaloneActions.ts:23-31 builds `selectionIds` from the whole selection and emits it; StudioModals.tsx:247 passes `saveAsComponentContext?.selectionIds[0]` as the modal's single elementId, with the acknowledgement at :238-240 ('a multi-selection contributes its first id').
fix: Wrap a multi-selection in a container before promoting it, or disable the action for multi-selections and say why.

finding: Cross-device master updates never propagate: the server hydrate is additive-only, so a device that already holds a master keeps its stale copy forever no matter how many times the master is edited elsewhere.
evidence: componentSync.ts:91-93 — `const localIds = new Set((await loadComponents(siteId)).map(c => c.id)); for (const r of remote) { if (localIds.has(r.componentId)) continue; }`. The mirror pushes every version up (mirrorComponentUpsert :47-62) and nothing ever pulls one down over an existing id.
fix: Compare `updatedAt`/`version` and pull when the remote is newer, or make the conflict visible instead of silently preferring local.
chain: Components -> ComponentDefinition -> update on device A -> siteComponents.upsert -> device B hydrate -> skipped, B keeps v1 forever

finding: siteComponents.usage has no caller, so 'which pages use this component?' is answerable and never asked — and the count the editor shows instead is scoped to the open site only, which is the wrong scope for a library that is shared across the workspace and can be deleted workspace-wide.
evidence: Router: site-component.ts:84-90. Callers: componentSync.ts uses upsert/delete/list/get; the dashboard uses workspaceList/workspaceRename/workspaceDelete (library-panel.tsx:24,37,46). The editor's own count comes from getInstancesOfComponent over the in-memory map (ComponentDetailScreen.tsx:247), which rehydrateInstances builds from `composer.elements.getAllElements()` (ComponentManager.ts:145) — every page of THIS site, no others. workspaceDelete removes the master from every site (site-component.ts:104-110) behind a UI that never calls usage.
fix: Call siteComponents.usage from the delete confirm in both surfaces and show the per-site breakdown before either delete runs (W-CO-06, W-O-14).
chain: Components -> ComponentDefinition -> Delete -> siteComponents.usage -> Delete confirm -> the user sees which sites and pages break

finding: Deleting a master is not on the undo stack, and undoing the canvas afterwards restores instance links to a component that no longer exists.
evidence: deleteComponent runs detachAllInstances then deleteFromStorage with no beginTransaction (ComponentManager.ts:389-406); the IndexedDB delete and the server mirror (useComponentSync.ts:51 → mirrorComponentDelete) are outside the engine snapshot entirely. History records from PROJECT_CHANGED snapshots of exportProject (HistoryManager.ts:93,191; captureSnapshot at :200), which carries element data — so a Cmd+Z restores `data.data.componentInstance` and rehydrateInstances (ComponentManager.ts:143-155) puts the entry back, pointing at a componentId `getComponent` now returns undefined for. syncInstance then returns NOT_SYNCED (ComponentInstances.ts:250) and VariantSection renders nothing (VariantSection.tsx:90).
fix: Either make delete undoable end to end (soft-delete the master, restore on undo — the TODO at ComponentDetailScreen.tsx:239 already says so), or drop the componentInstance data from the snapshot on delete so undo cannot resurrect a dangling link.

finding: An instance that fails to sync can never be re-synced by the user: syncInstance has no non-test caller, there is no 'out of date' indicator, and the only route back — Reset to master — throws the instance's own edits away.
evidence: syncInstance is exposed on the facade (ComponentManager.ts:462) and called only by syncAllInstances (ComponentInstances.ts:371) inside updateComponentMaster. A per-instance sync can fail and be swallowed: `if (!element) return NOT_SYNCED` / `if (!parent) return NOT_SYNCED` (:258-262) and the catch at :317. updateComponentMaster reports only `instancesSynced` (:284-289) and the toast says 'N instances followed' (ComponentDetailScreen.tsx:213-215) — it never says how many did not. The user's only remaining control is 'Reset to master' (VariantSection.tsx:150), which calls resetInstance, and that sets `overrides: []` (ComponentInstances.ts:346).
fix: Show an out-of-date badge when `instance.syncedVersion < component.version` (both are already stored) with a per-instance 'Update this copy' that calls syncInstance, and report the failure count in the update toast.
chain: Components -> ComponentInstance -> syncedVersion < version -> INSTANCE_SYNCED / an out-of-date badge -> Inspector instance band -> user can re-sync one copy without losing its edits

finding: Brand › Components never refreshes: its saved-component list is memoised on the composer identity, so creating, renaming or deleting a component leaves both the list and every instance count stale until the whole editor reloads.
evidence: ComponentsSection.tsx:125 `React.useMemo(() => getSavedComponents(composer), [composer])`; the per-row counts call getInstanceCount during render (:139, :191) with no subscription. The file imports no EVENTS and registers no composer listener, while the sibling panel does (useComponentsState.ts:160).
fix: Subscribe to COMPONENT_LIST_UPDATED (and the instance events from MOD-F-16) and re-read.

finding: Every row in Brand › Components draws a `›` chevron and has no onClick, while the panel's own footer states that 'every action here jumps to the Components panel to author'.
evidence: Catalog rows: `<Button color="light" data-catalog-card={component.id} className={ROW}>` with no handler (ComponentsSection.tsx:141-147); saved rows likewise (:194-201). Footer copy at :215-219. The chevron is in ROW's markup at :156 and :208.
fix: Wire both row kinds to the existing composer `ui:switch-tab` route the file already documents (:112-118), or drop the chevrons and the footer sentence.

finding: The command palette ships 'Toggle component view' with a printed ⌃⇧C shortcut that emits an event nothing listens to.
evidence: defaultCommands.ts:449-454 `run: () => composer.emit(EVENTS.UI_TOGGLE_COMPONENT_VIEW)`; UI_TOGGLE_COMPONENT_VIEW (events.ts:356) is named nowhere else in src/ — EVENT-GRAPH lists it under strong_orphans with mention only in engine:commands.
fix: Delete the command and the constant, or add the listener that toggles whatever 'component view' was meant to be.

finding: Component masters are the only editor entity stored under two different keys depending on load order — IndexedDB is opened with projectId 'default' at construction and re-keyed to the siteId later — so a component saved before the re-key lands in the wrong bucket.
evidence: ComponentManager constructs with `projectId = "default"` and calls initialize() → loadComponentsFromStorage() immediately (ComponentManager.ts:83,95-96,124). setProjectId(siteId) runs later, from useComposerInit.ts:158 and again from useComponentSync.ts:42. saveComponent stores `projectId` on the row (ComponentStorage.ts:94) and loadComponents filters on that index (:123-124).
fix: Pass the projectId into the constructor, or defer initialize() until setProjectId has run.

finding: Instance overrides are recorded on a positional path, so any structural edit to the master silently relocates or destroys them, and the only place that reports the loss is one toast on one screen.
evidence: Path shape `#/${elementPath}${elementPath ? "/" : ""}${type}/${property}` where elementPath is `children[i].children[j]` (ComponentInstances.ts:139-140, ComponentVariantResolver.ts:77). applyOverridesToTree returns `dropped` (ComponentInstances.ts:285) and the comment at :226-230 records that this used to reach only devError. Today exactly one caller surfaces it — ComponentDetailScreen.tsx:209-220. detachAllInstances, resetInstance and any future sync path do not.
fix: Key overrides by a stable node id copied from the master tree rather than by sibling index; until then, surface `overridesDropped` from every path that can produce it.

finding: Instances are re-keyed on every sync — the element is deleted and re-pasted with new ids — so anything holding an element id across a master update points at a node that no longer exists.
evidence: syncInstance calls `composer.elements.removeElement(elementId)` then `cloneWithNewIds(component.masterTree)` (which regenerates every id, ComponentInstances.ts:43-56) and pastes (:274-288); the instance map is re-keyed at :299-300. INSTANCE_SYNCED carries both ids (`instanceId`, `oldInstanceId`, :307-308) precisely so listeners can follow — and has none (MOD-F-16).
fix: Have selection, comments, animations and interactions listen to INSTANCE_SYNCED and remap, or preserve element ids across a sync where the master node is unchanged.

finding: Brand's own destinations already have a missing-screen wave (W-G) — not re-filed. The gap that wave could not see is the workspace half: no editor screen shows the shared theme's captured state, whether this site is themeLocked, or that a push has happened, although all three are server fields the editor could read.
evidence: Site.themeLocked and Workspace.sharedTheme/sharedThemeUpdatedAt exist (theme.service.ts:60-66, :117-127, listThemeTargets :107-113) and the editor's only reference to any of it is a link out: `window.open(`${DASHBOARD_URL}/dashboard/agency/theme`)` (DesignSystemTab.tsx:664). See W-G-01/02/03 for the root's own board defects.
fix: After MOD-F-01, read theme.getShared in the Brand root strip and show 'synced <when>' / 'locked — this site overrides the workspace theme' instead of a sentence that asserts a sync.

finding: Components' missing screens are already covered by W-O (W-O-08/09/10/11/12/13/14/15/18/20/21) and W-I-37/W-I-38 for the inspector's instance band — not re-filed. One state that wave did not name: there is no 'this master exists on the server but not on this device' state, which MOD-F-22 makes reachable.
evidence: hydrateComponentsFromServer skips any componentId already present locally (componentSync.ts:92) and returns a count that only drives a re-read (useComponentSync.ts:39-43); nothing renders 'N components pulled' or 'this copy is older than the shared one'.
fix: Surface the hydrate result and the version comparison in the Components panel header.
